findings.title: Reconfigure reports success but changes nothing once Options saved the Entities page
findings.claim: After one save of the Options flow's Entities page, a reconfigure that changes the indoor sensor and the weather entity aborts with reconfigure_successful while the effective configuration keeps both old values (2 of 2 changed keys shadowed; 0 on an entry with no options), and the reopened form is prefilled from entry.data rather than the running value.
findings.mechanism: _async_save_reconfigure writes the first screen's answers into entry.data only; the coordinator runs on {**entry.data, **entry.options}; the Entities options page (_OPTION_FIELDS rows with step 'entities') stores the same keys (price source/entity, token, weather, indoor, outdoor, ...) in entry.options, which then win over every later reconfigure. The prefill reads self._reconfigure_entry.data, so it also shows a value that is not running. D10-criteria Q2: the reconfiguration-flow row's done fails at this site.

evidence.unit: first-screen keys whose reconfigured answer is not the effective config
evidence.machine: local macOS box B2 (orchestrator machine), Python 3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: shared box, other finder seats running; a count, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb: wrap _async_save_reconfigure in memory so it also removes the first-screen keys from entry.options before writing entry.data

findings.metric_definition: shadowed = first-screen keys a reconfigure changed whose value in {**entry.data, **entry.options} after reconfigure_successful differs from the answer
findings.phenomenon_property: A reconfigure that reports success leaves every first-screen key it was given in force in the effective configuration the coordinator is built from, and the reconfigure form is prefilled from that effective configuration.

null_control.note: the same reconfigure on an entry whose options were never saved takes effect in full

reproduction_steps: Set up an entry (entity price source) with indoor sensor A and weather.home.
Options -> Entities: change the indoor sensor to B and save.
Entry menu -> Reconfigure: the form shows indoor A; choose C and weather.other; it reports success.
The coordinator still reads indoor B and weather.home.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: config_flow.py: the reconfigure write (and its prefill) operate on the effective configuration -- drop the written keys from entry.options in the same async_update_entry, and prefill from {**data, **options}

findings.title: Three ENERGY sensors publish state class measurement, a pair HA declares impossible
findings.claim: Lifetime Space Heating Energy, DHW Energy (lifetime) and Lifetime Total Energy publish device class energy with state class measurement (3 sensors), which Home Assistant's DEVICE_CLASS_STATE_CLASSES forbids (energy admits only total/total_increasing), so HA logs the impossible-state-class warning and the recorder compiles mean statistics instead of a sum, keeping them out of the Energy dashboard the README says they feed.
findings.mechanism: sensor._AccumulatingSensor declares _attr_state_class = SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT although its own docstring calls it the base of the TOTAL_INCREASING accumulators; the three cost subclasses override to TOTAL, the three energy subclasses inherit MEASUREMENT. The entity-device-class row's done (D10-criteria Q2) fails at these three sites: the device class is declared but HA rejects the pair.

evidence.unit: sensors with a (device_class, state_class) pair HA's table forbids
evidence.machine: local macOS box B2 (orchestrator machine), Python 3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: shared box, other finder seats running; a count, contention-immune

findings.metric_definition: impossible_pairs = sensors (all 62, via each platform's async_setup_entry) whose published device_class and state_class form a pair outside HA core's DEVICE_CLASS_STATE_CLASSES
findings.phenomenon_property: Every sensor's published (device_class, state_class) pair is one Home Assistant's DEVICE_CLASS_STATE_CLASSES admits; every lifetime kWh accumulator is total_increasing.
reproduction_steps: In HA core (homeassistant/components/sensor/entity.py) the state write logs 'is using state class measurement which is impossible considering device class (energy)'; sensor/recorder.py compiles mean/min/max for measurement, no sum.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: sensor.py: _AccumulatingSensor's state class TOTAL_INCREASING (the cost subclasses keep TOTAL)

findings.title: German run_optimization_no_prices message names {entry_id}; both raise sites pass entry_ids
findings.claim: Of 37 translated exception sites, 2 (button.py ForceOptimizationButton.async_press and services.py's run_optimization handler) raise run_optimization_no_prices with placeholder entry_ids while translations/de.json's message reads {entry_id}, so the German message's placeholders do not match the English one and HA's translation-placeholder validation drops it, showing German users the English text.
findings.mechanism: de.json exceptions.run_optimization_no_prices.message uses {entry_id}; strings.json, en.json and sv.json use {entry_ids}. HA validates a localized string's placeholders against the English ones on load (helpers/translation.py) and discards a mismatch. D10-criteria Q2: the exception-translations row's done fails at these two raise sites in one shipped language.

findings.title: Three degC difference sensors stay classless where HA >= 2025.11.0 offers TEMPERATURE_DELTA
findings.claim: ECL110 Displace, ECL110 Effective Displace and Prediction Accuracy publish temperature differences in degC with no device class (3 sensors); Home Assistant 2025.11.0 added SensorDeviceClass.TEMPERATURE_DELTA (measurement), so on any install at or above 2025.11.0 a device class is possible and unused, and a Fahrenheit user sees these deltas unconverted.
findings.mechanism: The rows were left bare deliberately because TEMPERATURE converts a delta as an absolute; the floor in hacs.json (2025.2.0) predates TEMPERATURE_DELTA (absent in core 2025.10.0's sensor/const.py, present from 2025.11.0). The rule asks for device classes where possible; a getattr(SensorDeviceClass, 'TEMPERATURE_DELTA', None) keeps the floor working. Per D10.M2 this is the todo needing an API newer than the floor, with its minimum release.

evidence.unit: sensors in degC with no device class
evidence.machine: local macOS box B2 (orchestrator machine), Python 3.14 venv-ci
evidence.contention_note: shared box, other finder seats running; a count, contention-immune

findings.metric_definition: delta_bare = sensors (via async_setup_entry) whose native unit is degC or K and whose published device class is None
findings.phenomenon_property: Every sensor publishing a temperature difference declares TEMPERATURE_DELTA wherever the running Home Assistant provides it, and none declares TEMPERATURE.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: sensor.py: the three delta sensors take SensorDeviceClass.TEMPERATURE_DELTA when the running core has it (getattr fallback to None at the 2025.2.0 floor)
